picks.title: Apple Watch Rethink Could See Debut of Round Model, Screenless Fitness Tracker, and More
picks.excerpt: Apple is re-evaluating the Apple Watch lineup and considering a host of radical new designs, according to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman. In today's edition of his "Power On" newsletter, Gurman compared plans for the Apple Watch's evolution to the "revolutionary design change" that the foldable iPhone represents. It will be "something that transforms the product for a new era".
picks.rationale: Freshest item in the pool and the biggest wearable form-factor signal of the week — a round watch and a screenless tracker means the whole watch-face/complication design language is up for renegotiation.

picks.title: No Ryzen AI: AMD launches Ryzen 5 439 and Ryzen 7 449 with binned NPUs
picks.excerpt: AMD has launched two new laptop chips, the Ryzen 5 439 and Ryzen 7 449, that quietly drop the NPU and the Ryzen AI branding found on their closest siblings.
picks.rationale: Directly actionable for anyone speccing a design workstation: same-looking Ryzen SKUs now ship with the NPU silently binned off, so local AI features quietly stop working on the cheaper machine.

picks.title: Google Home kicks off August with big app updates and a smarter Gemini for Home
picks.excerpt: Google Home's first August update is packed with useful new features, including AI Storytelling, improved alarms, and lots more.
picks.rationale: A shipped (not rumored) assistant update — AI Storytelling and reworked alarms show how Gemini for Home is being folded into everyday smart-home UI patterns rather than bolted on as a chatbot.

picks.title: Wacom's MovinkPad 11 is a fun, midpriced entry point for digital artists
picks.excerpt: The MovinkPad 11 a versatile little graphics tablet that can help make your wildest digital art dreams come true.
picks.rationale: The one pick that changes a designer's desk tomorrow — a standalone midpriced Wacom slate that removes the tethered-PC requirement from drawing hardware.

picks.title: SwitchBot Kata Friends AI Pet Review: Useless if You Don't Pay Up
picks.excerpt: A hands-on with SwitchBot's Kata Friends desktop AI pet: cute companion hardware whose personality and memory sit behind a subscription, exposing how AI gadget makers are pricing emotion as a service.
picks.rationale: Companion-robot hardware where the personality and memory live behind a paywall — a sharp case study in what happens when the emotional layer of a product becomes a subscription tier.
